title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both episodes) we produced N_pairs = 250 intents with gpt-5-mini and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Preregistration specified a sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast but that sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported inferential estimand applies only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps) because they can draft device CLI sequences from operator intents. Stochastic generation raises operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor CLI subtleties can yield unsafe changes. A common architectural mitigation interposes deterministic validators (e.g., header-space or state-snapshot checks) between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair; this generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern reduces mechanically verifiable errors in prior work [1],[2].

Open empirical questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs are already well-formed for constrained intents. Crucially, when the same generated candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), only downstream deterministic validation and allowed repairs can change paired outcomes. Our preregistered experiment quantifies that marginal verifier-and-single-repair effect on identical candidates. The final research question: When the same natural-language intent is realized by an LLM-generated configuration candidate and checked by a deterministic verifier, how large is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction between accepting the candidate (baseline) and applying a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair (guarded)? Our principal contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired estimate of that marginal effect for a constrained synthetic/emulation task partition.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and recent NetOps studies document active work on intent-to-configuration pipelines and on generate–verify architectures. Empirical NetOps evaluations show LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups but frequently require verification or human oversight for safety-critical properties [1],[3]. Deterministic network verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., header-space and model-checking derivatives) are widely used as validators in research and practice and can mechanize many syntactic and local-policy checks [4],[5]. Work on generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows in code and configuration domains reports improved detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects, though semantic correctness in heterogeneous production environments remains challenging [6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize filtering and validation layers but show adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [7].

Our study differs along three axes: (i) it uses a sealed preregistered paired design with explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics so the only possible paired changes are validator-detected and repair-driven; (ii) it reports stage-level provider-call reconciliation (shared initial generations and repair-stage counts) and reconciles model-call accounting against the adapter audit; and (iii) it archives deterministic validator traces and the analysis artifacts needed to reproduce the exact numeric outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the study as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and froze a confirmatory paired binary design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a single permitted automated repair per episode, and a primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. Concretely, for each intent we produced a single initial model generation (shared candidate) and reused that identical candidate in both baseline and guarded episodes. No independent first-pass generations were produced per condition; therefore any paired difference can arise only from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break, paired-link atomic changes). Tasks spanned difficulty labels medium/hard/very_hard and intentionally exercised typical NetOps workflow constraints.

Model invocation and guarded pipeline. The declared initial-generation model was gpt-5-mini for all shared initial calls (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e2...). For each guarded episode the pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: parse CLI, check required_sequence ordering, validate workflow constraints, and compare produced final_state to the task expected_final_state. If validator.valid == false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair (syntactic/ordering fixes only) and re-submitted the repaired candidate; no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed.

Preregistered exclusions and missingness. Exclusions removed items that deterministically prevented verification (vendor-parser failure), outputs with credential-like tokens, or denylist hits. The preregistered missingness plan allowed one immediate retry on API failure and prespecified sensitivity treatments treating excluded or incomplete pairs as failures. In the executed confirmatory partition no episodes were excluded and complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis plan. The primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) for the guarded − baseline paired difference. All analysis code and inputs are archived.
sections.results:
Execution reconciliation. The run completed planned_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs × 2 episodes) with completed_episode_count = 500, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}) consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics and the preregistered repair budget.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table observed: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in absolute proportion units (i.e., 0.0–1.2 percentage points). These numeric artifacts and the contingency CSV are archived for audit.

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes exhibit parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count encoded in task payloads (example: a hard task with parsed_command_count = 6 matched required_command_count = 6 and valid = true). Repair traces show deterministic syntactic/ordering edits; only one repair was required across 250 pairs.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and scope. Under the executed constrained synthetic/emulation partition and shared_initial_candidate semantics, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the sole failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 pp) bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.

Why the observed gain was small. Artifact-grounded causes include (1) constrained task templates and allowed_touched_fields that reduced intent ambiguity, (2) gpt-5-mini producing syntactically well-formed candidates for these constrained prompts, and (3) deterministic validator checks targeting mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, required final_state) rather than richer live-protocol behaviors.

Power and preregistered assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 pp effect with N = 250. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) substantially exceeded that assumption and consequently reduced power to detect small absolute improvements; therefore the paired-bootstrap CI is the most practically informative summary for the current conditions.

Threats to validity. Internal validity depends on prompt templates, registry of shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the single-repair policy. Construct validity is limited because the deterministic validator measures mechanically checkable properties and not protocol-level emergent correctness. External validity is limited: the executed confirmatory partition is synthetic/emulation only (the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast was not executed). Security/robustness to adaptive prompt-injection or production heterogeneity remain untested. These limitations constrain generalization.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (shared_initial_candidate semantics) on N_pairs = 250 constrained synthetic tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed a deterministic intent validator in 249/250 cases; inserting a validator plus one template-driven repair converted the single failing candidate, yielding a paired improvement of +0.4 pp (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). The executed inferential estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition; broader sim-to-real, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish operational generality. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and described in the Disclosure Statement so readers can reproduce the numeric reconciliation and inspect validator and repair traces.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and manifest pointer: declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The full archived evidence bundle and per-artifact manifests are available under the run's execution manifest (single manifest pointer): execution/execution_manifest.json in the archived evidence bundle (see preregistration and manifest hashes in the archive). Preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede. Immutable master-prompt reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Preregistered vs executed estimand: The preregistration specified multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Explicit deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported here is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Provider-call accounting in the archive reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Availability and auditability: analysis inputs, deterministic validator traces, repair traces, task manifest, raw responses, provider-call audits, and analysis CSVs referenced numerically in this paper are included in the archived evidence bundle pointed to by the single execution manifest. Readers may inspect the archived manifest to recover the full per-file manifests and hashes; per-file paths and exhaustive per-artifact hashes are retained in the archive rather than reproduced here to preserve concision in this Disclosure Statement.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.
Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected final_state) but did not measure protocol-level emergent behaviors or runtime forwarding semantics.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not tested and remain open threats.
